item.text:
**6B.7 Research Note**
Verdict: mixed, leaning no. I found several signs that Egypt’s biggest cash-transfer and social-support channels were more formalized than patronage-based in 2024, but I found stronger evidence that vulnerable groups still faced exclusion, and that economic complaints were met with coercion rather than neutral welfare administration. I did not find strong direct evidence that Sisi systematically used food, housing, jobs, or benefits as explicit loyalty rewards in 2024; the stronger evidence is indirect, through exclusion and punishment.

**Positive / less patronage-like**
- **Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report - Public Investment Management Assessment** — IMF — 2024-04-02 — [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051)  
  The IMF says Egypt had already taken steps to improve infrastructure access and public investment management through new legislation, information systems, and staff-capacity work, alongside Education 2.0 and health-infrastructure rollout. This supports a technocratic, rules-based service-delivery reading rather than pure patronage.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.5`, `6B.6`

- **Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs** — World Bank — 2024-05-28 — [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs)  
  Takaful and Karama is described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and run with proxy means testing, a grievance mechanism, and a dynamic social registry. That is strong evidence against crude loyalty-buying through welfare, though it does not prove political neutrality in all cases.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`

- **Egypt’s economic strategy for 2024-2030** — State Information Service — 2024 — [URL](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/factbox-egypts-economic-strategy-for-2024-2030/)  
  The official strategy framed large-scale expansion of Takaful/Karama, pensions, micro-projects for poor families, and coverage for irregular workers as structured social policy. This is official self-presentation, but it does show a policy design language more consistent with broad support than with selective patronage alone.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.6`, `6B.4`

- **House of Representatives approves drafted Social Solidarity bill** — State Information Service — 2024-12-01 — [URL](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/house-of-representatives-approves-drafted-social-solidarity-bill/)  
  The bill aimed to unify support programs, regulate government grants, and define eligibility rules for Takaful and Karama. That is evidence of formalization and administrative rules, not obviously of ad hoc rewards for loyalty.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.4`, `6B.6`

- **Launch of Joint UN programme under the Joint Platform for Migrants and Refugees in Egypt** — UNHCR Egypt — 2024-09-30 — [URL](https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/launch-joint-un-programme-under-joint-platform-migrants-and-refugees-egypt)  
  Egypt, the UN, and the EU launched a program to support health and education for refugees and migrants in vulnerable situations after the Sudan influx. That is a real inclusion signal, not a loyalty test.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.6`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Negative / patronage-like or exclusionary**
- **Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis** — Amnesty International — 2024-05-13 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/)  
  Amnesty documented arrests of protesters, striking workers, and online critics over complaints about price hikes and the cost of living. That is not direct proof of welfare being used as a loyalty tool, but it shows the state responding to hardship complaints with punishment rather than neutral service correction.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.5`, `6B.6`

- **Egypt: New law threatens to reduce access to healthcare for millions** — Amnesty International — 2024-07-30 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-new-law-threatens-to-reduce-access-to-healthcare-for-millions/)  
  Amnesty said Law 87 of 2024 privatized management of public health facilities without price regulation and was rushed through without adequate consultation. This is strong contrary evidence on access and affordability, and it weakens a clean non-patronage reading.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.6`, `6B.5`

- **Egypt: Education Restricted for Refugees** — Human Rights Watch — 2024-12-02 — [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees)  
  HRW found tens of thousands of refugee and asylum-seeking children out of school because of residency requirements, fees, discrimination, and limited free public education. That is direct evidence of exclusionary access rules affecting a vulnerable group.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.6`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Egypt authorities must end campaign of mass arrests and forced returns of Sudanese refugees** — Amnesty International — 2024-06-19 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-authorities-must-end-campaign-of-mass-arrests-and-forced-returns-of-sudanese-refugees/)  
  Border forces and police mass-arrested Sudanese refugees, held women, men, and children in cruel conditions, and forced returns without asylum access. That is strong evidence of punitive treatment of a vulnerable displaced group, not neutral welfare administration.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.6`, `6B.3`

- **President al-Sisi must reject new asylum law which violates refugee rights** — Amnesty International — 2024-12-03 — [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/egypt-president-al-sisi-must-reject-new-asylum-law-which-violates-refugee-rights/)  
  Amnesty said the asylum law restricted rights, lacked due process, and failed to protect education, housing, and social security for refugees and asylum seekers. This cuts against the idea that social support was being administered in a rights-preserving, non-punitive way.  
  QIDs: `6B.7`, also `6B.6`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong direct 2024 evidence that Sisi explicitly used food, housing, jobs, permits, or benefits as individualized political rewards or punishments in the way some patronage systems do.
- The evidence I did find is mostly indirect: formalization of cash transfers on one side, and exclusionary or punitive treatment of critics, refugees, and service complainants on the other.
- So the safest reading is not “cleanly yes” or “cleanly no,” but “some institutionalization existed, yet the broader system still showed coercive and exclusionary distribution patterns.”
